model: A job I would never do is working as an emergency-room nurse. To be honest, I've always admired nurses, but I know I'm just not cut out for it. My cousin has been working in the emergency department of a big hospital in Ho Chi Minh City for about five years, so I've heard a lot about what it's really like. First of all, nurses often work unsociable hours. My cousin has done countless night shifts, and she's missed most family celebrations since she started. The job is also physically demanding, because she's on her feet for twelve hours at a time, lifting patients and running between rooms. But the main reason is the stress. In an emergency room, some decisions are literally a matter of life and death, and you're under constant pressure. You have to keep a cool head when people are shouting, crying or seriously injured. I've never been good in a crisis. Even when I've cut my finger in the kitchen, I've nearly fainted, so I can't imagine dealing with car accident victims every night. I can also see how the job has taken its toll on my cousin. She's often exhausted, and she's been thinking about changing to a quieter clinic. So I'd never choose that career myself, but I have a lot of respect for the people who do it, because they're real heroes.
